title: Partition full Python and WebView discovery
summary: Run complete Python, non-browser WebView, and individually isolated browser-backed unittest partitions in hosted CI, remove redundant codex-branch push runs, and make the observed Launch/Reports browser assertions wait for their authoritative fixture states.
reason: Hosted full-discovery attempts failed on different browser modules after long aggregate runs, while every unchanged module passed independently. Separating the roots removed Chromium ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE, then fresh-process jobs exposed two test synchronization defects: Launch awaited the coalescing refresh wrapper, which can return before a queued refresh, and Reports asserted an early actionable posture after the smoke intentionally transitioned its review boards to historical-unavailable state. The final changes preserve every assertion at the state where its contract applies.
behavior_before: Deep Audit and Generated Drift originally ran all 3,139 tests in one Python process; an initial two-root partition still ran 239 WebView tests in one process. Late browser/CDP tests failed non-deterministically, culminating in Chromium ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE on the hosted runner.
behavior_after: Each workflow runs the complete tests/python root, all 31 non-browser WebView modules together, and every one of the 23 browser-backed modules in its own fresh Python process. Launch explicitly awaits refreshAllNow for the home evidence set, including sample validation and backend preflight, before checking readiness. Reports verifies Action needed immediately after loading its actionable fixture and separately verifies historical-unavailable review boards after later lifecycle operations. Generated Drift and CodeQL run once for codex pull requests and again after merge through retained main push triggers. No test, browser timeout, permission, required context, or safety assertion is removed or weakened.
manual_validation: OBSERVED: hosted failures rotated across Launch/Queue, Diagnostics handoff, Settings/Launch, Rename, Completed/Pending proof, and High Risk, demonstrating process-lifetime/resource sensitivity rather than one product assertion.

OBSERVED: the first hosted per-module run removed ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE but exposed Launch waiting on an intermediate coalesced refresh and Reports checking Action needed after its final historical-unavailable transition.

OBSERVED: the later single Generated Drift run passed all 2,900 Python tests, then failed three late browser modules with Chromium ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE after 372 seconds, motivating per-browser-module process isolation.
PASS: every browser module that failed in hosted aggregate discovery passed unchanged in local isolated/full-browser runs.

PASS: exact final CI partition locally in 424.9s: 2,900 Python tests with one expected skip, 210 non-browser WebView tests, and all 29 browser-backed tests across 23 fresh processes; 3,139 total with no omitted tests.
PASS: focused final Launch/Queue and Maintenance/Reports browser modules, 3 tests in 16.376s; no timeout increase, retry, skip, or safety-assertion removal.
PASS: full tests/webview root passed 239 tests, including all 29 browser-backed tests.
PASS: identical partitioned discovery locally; tests/python and tests/webview both passed, preserving all 3,139 tests with one expected skip.
PASS: partitioned hosted Deep Audit Python unit-test job passed all tests in 11m37s.
rollback_plan: Restore the single discovery command only if a future runner proves it stable under equivalent browser load. Do not compensate by increasing timeouts or skipping browser tests.
notes:
The required check names and workflow permissions are unchanged. This is execution isolation within each existing Python unit-test job plus removal of redundant push/pull_request duplication on codex PR heads, not a reduction in test scope. Main push and pull-request validation remain enabled. Launch now awaits the non-coalescing refreshAllNow path for deterministic evidence. Reports retains both the initial actionable-fixture assertion and the final historical-unavailable assertions.
